title: Your backflow test failed. Repair is only step one.
description: Move from failure code to repair, passing retest, and accepted submission without losing the local deadline.
prompt: What do you have right now?
answer: A failed field result usually remains open until the required repair is completed, the assembly passes a retest, and the result is accepted through the utility's workflow.
urgency: Use the deadline and utility named on the actual notice. National guidance cannot supply a local repair window.
diagramAlt: Four-stage failed backflow test workflow from report to accepted submission
identifiers: Failure code or component: check valve, relief valve, air inlet, or shutoff issue.
Deadline: printed on the notice, portal, or utility program page.
Submitter: some utilities require the accepted tester to file the result.

choices.label: I have the failed test sheet
choices.detail: Keep the code, measured values, tester, device ID, and date together.

choices.label: The repair is complete
choices.detail: The next questions are passing retest and accepted submission.

choices.label: The deadline is close or unknown
choices.detail: Find the utility record before scheduling the remaining steps.

choices.label: I need repair or retest help
choices.detail: Send the failure context, not just a request for a generic test.

steps.title: Read the failed component
steps.body: Use the tester's code and measurements; do not reduce the report to only pass or fail.

steps.title: Repair the actual failure
steps.body: The service scope should match the assembly, model, body condition, and failed component.

steps.title: Complete the retest
steps.body: A repaired assembly is not proven compliant until the required test passes.

steps.title: Confirm accepted submission
steps.body: Keep portal confirmation, accepted form, or other proof required by the utility.

safeChecks: Photograph or scan the failure sheet.
Record the notice deadline and utility contact.
Confirm whether the repair quote includes retest and filing.
stopConditions: The assembly protects fire service or a critical commercial use
The device is visibly cracked or actively discharging
The proposed provider cannot meet the utility tester gate
notThisDevice: A repair invoice alone is not proof of a passing retest.
A portal account alone does not prove the report was accepted.
A national directory does not override an official approved-tester list.
evidenceNote: Local deadlines, tester eligibility, and submission rules come only from the governing utility record and its official sources.
